decision: Delete core after splitting object, bucket, provider I/O, transfer, usage, and project-maintenance ownership
reason: ObjectManager is a route-wide aggregate with 116 declared methods; a rename preserves the broad constructor
verification: No core imports or ObjectManager route parameters; focused domain tests and full suite pass

decision: Use distinct RecordID, ContentID, Record, and CanonicalContent values
reason: A physical persisted record and a prepared same-checksum view have different identity and listing semantics
verification: Raw-record and canonical-content tests preserve stable IDs, replicas, aliases, public state, and maintenance prepared listings

decision: Keep generated API values and codecs in HTTP adapters
reason: InternalObject embeds generated DRS and owns observable custom JSON behavior
verification: No generated imports in domain or persistence; wire tests preserve id/did, hashes, retired fields, aliases, and unknown properties

decision: Delete internal/db and put narrow ports beside consumers
reason: The 18 interfaces combine unrelated capabilities; consumers use different subsets and backends only assert the aggregate
verification: No internal/db imports; both adapters satisfy every listed consumer port; optimized and fallback tests pass

decision: Keep SQLite and PostgreSQL as separate persistence adapters
reason: Their locks, placeholders, JSON/time types, transactions, and upgrade behavior differ materially
verification: Both focused suites pass; live PostgreSQL runs when DSN is available and any skip is recorded

decision: Merge session and policy under internal/access and separate authentication integrations
reason: Policy immediately consumes the session, while middleware mixes Fiber with local, Gen3, JWT, and process mechanisms
verification: No old auth/authz imports; access has no Fiber/core/DB dependency; middleware and server auth tests pass

decision: Make buckets the only credential, scope, visibility, cache, and invalidation owner
reason: Current bucket catalog owns CRUD/cache, while providers need only credential lookup
verification: No buckets-to-storage-parent or buckets-to-objects edge; cache and optimized/fallback visibility tests pass

decision: Use storage/address as the shared leaf and let storage lookup return bucket-owned values
reason: Buckets and storage need the same provider/scheme/bucket-key syntax without a cycle or duplicate credential DTO
verification: Address imports stdlib only; alias matrix passes; storage imports no bucket service and parent imports no provider child

decision: Move URL signing, multipart, probe, inventory, and deletion I/O to storage with provider children
reason: urlmanager and signer split one provider system, while core directly owns a second set of provider SDK operations
verification: No old imports; provider contract suites pass without expiry, range, ordering, fallback, cache, or file-root changes

decision: Put event/grant values and identity in usage; put access and multipart orchestration in transfers
reason: Accounting/report consumers share event identity, while transfer workflow composes objects, buckets, storage, and a recorder
verification: No usage-to-transfers edge; event/grant identity matches both SQL dialects; issuance and metrics route tests pass

decision: Move pending LFS state and workflow to transfers; keep protocol behavior in httpapi/lfs
reason: The current LFS server mixes generated response/media contracts with target, multipart, pending-row, and accounting work
verification: Generated LFS response tests, old pending-row round trips, multipart flow, and route tests pass

decision: Put scope repair in maintenance/scoperepair and project inspection/cleanup in maintenance/projectstorage
reason: These workflows combine object records, bucket visibility/scopes, and provider I/O, so none of those lower-level domains can own them
verification: Maintenance has no generated imports; prepared listing, inspection, inventory comparison, cleanup, and bulk-delete contracts pass unchanged

decision: Split internal HTTP packages by workflow and keep a tiny explicit mount owner
reason: internaldrs recursively mounts unrelated records, transfers, buckets, inspection, and repair; a namespace rename would retain it
verification: Exact method/path/alias/order parity; zero routeutil and old API imports; generated DRS adoption remains deferred

decision: Delete common and models after symbol-level migration
reason: They share representations and helpers across unrelated owners; keeping residue would restore accidental coupling
verification: Zero imports; common destination contracts and object/bucket/usage wire tests pass

decision: Rename crypto to credentialcipher but preserve dynamic key selection during structural moves
reason: Every operation is credential-specific and currently re-reads manager/key environment, which is observable behavior
verification: V1, V2, plaintext, purpose string, audit, and per-operation environment behavior remain green

decision: Keep config environment export and plugin inheritance until a separate characterized behavior change
reason: LoadConfig mutates parent process state and plugin subprocesses inherit it; deleting the bridge during reorganization changes behavior
verification: File/env precedence, successive loads, mock fallback, and child plugin inheritance are pinned before any later removal

decision: Delete internal/testutils in favor of one SQLite fixture and consumer-local fakes
reason: The broad mock implements unrelated database and URL behavior and supplies defaults that can hide missing wiring
verification: No testutils imports; no production testsupport dependency; each fake implements only its consumer port

decision: Keep internal/version and its linker contract unchanged
reason: The package is cohesive and moving it would change Makefile -X paths without improving ownership
verification: Version command output and release linker flags remain valid
